methodology: Bounded source-critical first-pass: Qur'an Arabic and translation 12:11–15 checked against Hebrew Masoretic display and Revised JPS 2023 Genesis 37:12–17; other Genesis locators remain candidates requiring critical checks. Reviewed prior PR #423 and main, avoided duplicate verse keys. Not a comprehensive review; no claims of direct literary dependence. No Supabase write.

verses.summary: Brothers ask why Jacob does not trust them with Joseph; Genesis 37:12–14 instead has Jacob initiate Joseph's trip to check on his brothers.
Brothers request Joseph accompany them for play and promise protection; Genesis 37:12–14 depicts a mission to check the brothers and flocks, not recreation.
Jacob fears a wolf might devour Joseph; Genesis 37:33 later has Jacob infer a wild beast killed Joseph after seeing the garment, without an advance warning.
Brothers insist their strong group could protect Joseph from a wolf; Genesis 37 does not record this exchange.

Brothers put Joseph in a well/pit; Genesis 37:23–24 narrates stripping Joseph's garment and placing him in an empty pit. Qur'an additionally reports divine reassurance that Joseph will later confront them.

candidates.difference: In the Qur'an brothers request permission; in Genesis Jacob sends Joseph to check the flocks.
candidates.verification: Hebrew Masoretic text and Revised JPS 2023 inspected on Sefaria; Greek/Syriac and manuscript collation not completed.

dossier.title: Joseph's departure, the wolf warning and the pit
dossier.chronology: Qur'an 12:11–15 presents the brothers' persuasion of Jacob, his wolf warning, their promise, the placement in a well and divine reassurance. Genesis 37:12–24 presents Jacob sending Joseph to locate the brothers, the journey via Shechem and Dothan, and the brothers placing him in a pit.

source_table.edition: Sefaria Hebrew Masoretic text / Revised JPS 2023 translation

dossier.similarities: Joseph travels toward his brothers; brothers place him in a pit; animal-death explanation occurs in the larger story.
dossier.differences: Genesis has Jacob send Joseph and later infer animal attack; Qur'an has brothers request the trip and Jacob fear a wolf beforehand. Qur'an 12:15 includes a revelation not narrated in Genesis 37:23–24.
dossier.witnesses: Hebrew Masoretic text displayed with Revised JPS 2023 at Sefaria. Greek Septuagint, Syriac Peshitta, rabbinic and other later retellings not collated.
dossier.dating: The Genesis literary tradition predates Islam, but composition/redaction chronology must not be equated with the dates of surviving manuscript witnesses. Specific manuscript attestations have not been audited.
dossier.interpretations: Shared Joseph narrative with meaningful plot differences; no conclusion about direct textual borrowing or route of transmission.
